From Wiktionary, the free dictionary
See also: Chips, CHiPs, and CHIPS

English

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /t͡ʃɪps/
  • Audio (US):(file)
  • Rhymes: -ɪps

Verb

[edit]

chips

  1. third-person singular simple present indicative of chip

Noun

[edit]

chips

  1. plural of chip

Noun

[edit]

chips (plural chips)

  1. (slang) A carpenter.
    • 1847 March 30, Herman Melville, Omoo: A Narrative of Adventures in the South Seas; […], London: John Murray, […], →OCLC:
      But the Saturday-night bottles were not all. The carpenter and cooper, in sea parlance, Chips and Bungs, who were the "Cods," or leaders of the forecastle, in some way or other, managed to obtain an extra supply […]
    • 1929, The Atlantic Monthly, volume 144, page 462:
      I began a new branch of experience by going to sea as a 'chips.'

Related terms

[edit]
  • brother chip

Anagrams

[edit]
  • SCHIP

French

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from English chips.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ʃips/
  • (Canada) IPA(key): /tʃip/
  • Audio (France):(file)

Noun

[edit]

chips f or m or m pl (sometimes plural only, in variation, invariable)

  1. (Anglicism) chips (American English), crisps (British English)
    • 2006 November 21, “Regard [Glare]”, in デスノート [Death Note], spoken by Light Yagami (Alexis Tomassian), Nice Fellow, via MCM:
      Puis je prends une chips, que je mange!
      Then I'll take a chip, which I'll eat!

Usage notes

[edit]
  • Feminine in France, masculine in Belgium and masculine plural in some older dictionaries.

Further reading

[edit]
  • “chips”, in Trésor de la langue française informatisé [Digitized Treasury of the French Language], 2012
